title: Alternate-route orchestrator for version-locked models (region & variant routing, deprecation TTLs)
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Design and implement an 'alternate-route orchestrator' service that transparently redirects requests for version-locked (version-locked = customer pinned) models to compatible alternatives when the primary version is unavailable, deprecated, or capacity constrained. Goals: keep API behavior stable for customers who pin a model version, preserve latency SLOs when possible, offer clear observability and audit trail of any redirect, and enforce safe deprecation windows so customers can migrate with notice. This ticket covers policy engine, routing decisions, TTL-based deprecation handling, variant compatibility mapping, per-region routing rules, and runtime metrics/alerts.
comments: 2025-01-15: Ticket created after postmortem from incident-2025-01-09 where a pinned model version caused widespread 503s in eu-west. Raised by SRE and AE teams.

2025-01-18: Architecture review with runtime and routing leads. Decided to implement orchestrator as a lightweight policy layer in front of the existing router rather than modifying the serving runtime; reduces blast radius and simplifies rollback.

2025-01-22: Prototype for 'compatibility map' data model completed. Stores tuples of (model_family, version, variant_fingerprint) -> list of fallback candidates ordered by suitability score. Prototype lives in github.com/redwood/runtime/fallback-proto.

2025-01-25: Key decision: 'soft redirect' by default (respond with 200 from fallback model and add X-Model-Redirect header) vs 'hard redirect' (return 503 with suggestion) — we will default to soft redirects for non-SLA customers and provide a strict opt-in for tenants that require explicit failure instead of automatic fallback.

2025-01-29: Observability requirements drafted. Must emit metric routed.fallback.count, routed.fallback.latency.delta, routed.deprecation.notice_sent and an audit event with original_version, target_version, region, route_policy, and reason.
2025-02-01: Implementation started. Diego paired with Luca on policy engine; Priya to add migration runbook and customer notification templates. Unblocked by token-mapping change from ENG-8273.

2025-02-01: Blocker identified: need canonical mapping of variant fingerprints from model-onboarding pipeline (research to provide stable fingerprinting by 2025-02-10). Added dependency ENG-57201 (research fingerprinting).
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine can evaluate a fallback decision within 2ms p50 and 10ms p99 on the routing path under normal load
Request flow supports transparent soft-redirects: responses from fallback model include X-Redwood-Fallback: true and X-Redwood-Original-Version headers
Fallback selection respects: region affinity, latency budget, compute-cost tiers, and explicit per-tenant blacklist/allowlist

Deprecation TTLs enforced: when runtime emits a 'deprecate-start' signal, we send first notification to tenant contacts, start soft-redirecting after configurable grace_period, and hard-fail only after final_ttl expires
All fallback events are logged to the audit stream and surface in Console's Rollout and Model pages with counts and latency deltas
E2E test harness demonstrates fallback for: regional outage, variant incompatibility, and explicit model deprecation with metrics validated
Feature flagging exists so we can turn orchestrator on per-org for rollout and immediate emergency cutoff
implementation_notes: Architecture: orchestrator service sits in the control plane router path as a stateless decision service. It fetches compatibility maps and tenant overrides from a read-through cache (Redis) refreshed via streaming updates from model catalog service.

Compatibility scoring: combine model semantic compatibility (trained tokenizer + architecture fingerprint), performance profile similarity (latency, memory), and cost multiplier. Compute a single suitability score to rank candidates.

Deprecation signals: model-catalog will emit events: deprecate-start, deprecate-enforce. Orchestrator tracks per-version deprecation metadata: notice_sent, soft_redirect_start, hard_redirect_start timestamps.
Region rules: prefer same-region compatible variants; allow cross-region redirect only if latency delta < 30ms and tenant region-policy permits cross-region failover.

Tenant opt-in/opt-out: per-tenant flags: allow_automatic_fallback (bool), allow_cross_region (bool), strict_failure_mode (bool). Defaults: allow_automatic_fallback=true for free and standard accounts; false for strict-enterprise unless opted-in.

Observability: enrich spans with fallback.reason and fallback.candidate_version; create Grafana dashboards and PagerDuty alerts when fallback rate > 1% p5 for any org or >0.1% global sustained over 10m.
Performance: policy cache warmed on pod start; policy evaluation implemented in Rust for low-latency integration with the router. Fallback decisions are idempotent and safe for retries.

Security: audit events stored in existing audit-log pipeline with KMS-encrypted payloads for Private customers. No model weights move through orchestrator — decisions only reference model identifiers and routes.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature gated off. Deploy orchestrator to dev and staging clusters; run synthetic traffic mimicking pinned workloads.
Phase 1: Enable soft-redirects for internal orgs only (canary) and monitor fallback metrics for 48h. Verify audit logs and Console surfaces.
Phase 2: Gradual rollout to 5% of external tenants with allow_automatic_fallback=true for 7 days. Send deprecation notices via email + in-console banners for any auto-redirect occurrences.
Phase 3: Enable by default for all non-strict tenants; publish docs and migration guide. Keep strict-enterprise opt-out preserved.
Phase 4: Enable cross-region fallback for tenants that opted-in; monitor tail-latency and billing delta metrics closely.
Emergency: feature flag to disable orchestrator globally and re-route to legacy behavior within 30s
test_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation logic and TTL transitions
Integration test: simulate model unavailability in eu-west and assert redirect to eu-central candidate within latency budget
Chaos test: kill serving nodes for a pinned version and assert orchestrator emits audit events and that soft-redirect rate spikes appropriately
Regression test: ensure no fallback occurs when tenant's strict_failure_mode=true
Load test: policy decision throughput at 20k req/s with p99 latency < 10ms for decision path
